      type: object

          minLength: 1

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison

            spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and country code
            are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and is the value stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current

I implemented the `customerCode` assignment feature, formatted `<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, across the standard Spring layers:

1. **`Owner` entity** (`model/Owner.java`) — added a persisted `customerCode` field mapped to a new `customer_code` column, with getter/setter.

   - **LAST3** = first three letters of `lastName`, upper-cased (`Locale.ROOT`).
   - **NNNN** = `findAllOwners().size() + 1`, zero-padded to 4 digits (`%04d`).

Since assignment happens per create and the count reflects previously-persisted owners (JPA auto-flushes before the query), each new owner's sequence is exactly one greater than the previous — satisfying the test's global-sequence assertion (e.g. `SMI-0011` then `JON-0012`).
